Lemma
Source: chow-knopf-ricci-flow:page-0039, chow-knopf-ricci-flow:page-0040, chow-knopf-ricci-flow:page-0041 1. Lemma 2.7\group eternal-solutions

Up to homothety, the cigar soliton is the unique rotationally symmetric gradient Ricci soliton of positive curvature on $\R ^2$.

Proof

Source: chow-knopf-ricci-flow:page-0039, chow-knopf-ricci-flow:page-0040, chow-knopf-ricci-flow:page-0041 \sketch Write a rotationally symmetric metric as $g=ds^2+\varphi (s)^2\, d heta ^2$. Using the orthonormal frame $e_1=\partial _s$, $e_2=\varphi ^{-1}\partial _ heta $, the connection satisfies $\omega ^2_1=\varphi '(s)\, d heta $, so the curvature is $K=-\varphi ''/\varphi $. For a radial potential $f=f(s)$, the steady gradient soliton equation $Kg= abla abla f$ reduces to

\[ f''=- rac{\varphi ''}{\varphi },\qquad rac{\varphi ' f'}{\varphi }=- rac{\varphi ''}{\varphi }. \]

Hence $f'=\alpha \varphi $ for a constant $\alpha eq 0$, and convexity forces $\alpha >0$. Substituting back gives $\varphi ''+2a^2\varphi \varphi '=0$, so $\varphi '+a^2\varphi ^2=b$. Smoothness at the origin requires $\varphi (0)=0$ and $\varphi '(0)=1$, forcing $b=1$. Thus $\varphi (s)=a^{-1} anh (as)$, and after the rescaling $\sigma =as$ one gets $g=a^{-2}g_\Sigma $.
